messages:
Michelle (Marketing): heads-up — incident on hosted inference in us-west-2. ops just flagged higher latencies and some 5xx spikes. need marketing-to-ops comms plan for customer-facing copy + lead routing. who can take the first draft?

Raj (Growth): I can draft quick status page copy and an email snippet. timeline? do we want an immediate short update then a follow-up? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Dave (Oncall): ETA for mitigation ~30–45m, rollback window if needed. prefer a short status page now: acknowledge, scope, and ETA. avoid technical root cause until postmortem.

Elaine (Support): routing note — we should flag Dedicated customers + private deploys separately (they often have different SLAs). Also add a contact channel for high-sev customers (support@redwood.ai / account team).

Michelle (Marketing): good call. Raj: please include two variants: public short (status page + twitter-length) and an account-facing email with dedicated customer wording. Also need EU-friendly timestamp text for EMEA customers.

Raj (Growth): sharing first pass in thread. please react with :thumbsup: if ok or comment.

Raj (Growth): ```Status: Degraded performance in us-west-2 (Hosted API) — We’re seeing elevated latency and errors affecting text generation. Scope: A subset of hosted API customers in us-west-2. What we’re doing: Our on-call team is actively investigating and working to restore normal operation. ETA: next update in 30 minutes. If you rely on Dedicated or Private deployments, your service is not expected to be affected; if you are seeing issues, please contact support@redwood.ai.```

Dave (Oncall): looks good. change: "not expected to be affected" -> "should not be affected" (softer). Also add a line about failover to other regions if customers have multi-region routing.

Elaine (Support): for account email draft add: "If your production traffic is routed to us-west-2 and you need assistance, reply to this email and we’ll loop in your account engineer." Keep tone empathetic.

Michelle (Marketing): Nina (Legal) — can you take a 10-min look for any compliance phrasing we need (no promises about SLA, avoid admitting data exposure)? @Nina

Nina (Legal): quick read — language looks safe. Recommend removing phrase "working to restore" and replace with "investigating" in the public copy to avoid implying timelines. Also add: "We will provide a full incident report after investigation."

incidents-bot: Incident #INC-2028: Severity 2 — us-west-2 latency spike. Channel: #incidents. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2028

Raj (Growth): updated copy below with edits from Dave + Nina + Elaine. please confirm ASAP so we can post.

Raj (Growth): ```Public status page (brief):
We are investigating elevated latency and errors impacting a subset of hosted API customers in us-west-2. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will post an update within 30 minutes and provide a full incident report after investigation.
If you are experiencing issues and are on Dedicated or Private deployments, please contact support@redwood.ai and your account team.```

Michelle (Marketing): good. plan for channels: 1) Status page now 2) Tweet + short LinkedIn post echoing status page 3) Account email to active Dedicated customers 4) In-product banner for affected tenants (ops to decide). Who will post status page?

Dave (Oncall): ops will publish status page. I’ll also trigger an in-product banner for affected hosted customers. ETA 4m.

Elaine (Support): I’ll pull list of Dedicated customers hitting us-west-2 and prepare the account email list. Can marketing draft the email subject and snippet?

Michelle (Marketing): Draft subject options: "We’re investigating service degradation in us-west-2" or "Redwood: Investigating elevated latency in us-west-2". leaning toward the first.

Raj (Growth): email snippet: "Hello — we’re investigating elevated latency impacting some workloads in us-west-2. Our team is investigating; we’ll share updates as we have them. If this affects your production systems, reply to this message and we’ll prioritize support."

Nina (Legal): recommend adding: "No customer data has been compromised to our knowledge at this time." (only if ops confirms)

Dave (Oncall): confirming — no evidence of data compromise. fine to include Nina's sentence.

Michelle (Marketing): timeline: status page + tweet in next 5m; account email within 20m; follow-up postmortem plan in thread after incident is resolved. Raj + Elaine own the account email. Dave will own ops updates. Nina will sign off final copy.

Raj (Growth): posting status page in 2m. I’ll ping once live.

incidents-bot: Status update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2028 — initial message live

Raj (Growth): status page live. pushing tweet now.

Michelle (Marketing): thanks team. after the incident, we should run a short internal retro on the customer messaging timeline and update the marketing incident playbook with the Dedicated-customer escalation step. adding as action item. :memo:
